title: [review] local-fact: verify over received wire bytes, not re-encoded claims (C/Rust interop)
description: Correctness+edge finding on viku.4 (local_facts.py). verify_local_fact re-encodes claims via to_cbor() and rebuilds the protected header, then verifies; from_cose_sign1 discards the received protected/payload bstrs. RFC 9052 §4.4 signs the payload bstr AS TRANSPORTED. A fact validly signed by a C/Rust encoder with different map-key order (canonical/length-first), non-minimal int, indefinite-length map, or an extra protected-header entry decodes fine but verifies False — Python↔C/Rust interop break. Fix: retain received protected/payload on LocalFact during decode and verify over those bytes. Also note spec 8.13.1 mandates no canonical/deterministic encoding and no test/vectors pinning exists; consider spec+vector-pinning the exact encoding. Sibling delegation_tokens.verify_delegation_token has the same re-encode pattern (codebase-wide convention question).
close_reason: Fixed: LocalFact retains received protected/payload bstrs (from_cose_sign1, issue_local_fact); verify_local_fact and to_cose_sign1 use them verbatim per RFC 9052 4.4; re-encode fallback kept for field-constructed facts. 3 new tests (foreign-order claims + extra protected entry signed independently, byte-stable reserialize, unpaired-bstr rejection); all 3 confirmed RED on old code, GREEN on fix; 30/30 local-fact tests pass; gateway+crypto suites show zero delta vs unmodified baseline (13 pre-existing failures unrelated). 3x reviewer-model codereview: correctness PASS, security PASS, edge pass filed 2 follow-ups (replace-desync P2, to_cose_sign1 fallback coverage P3) + 2 bead-described follow-ups (delegation re-encode P2, vector pinning P3) + 1 pre-existing lora_medium breakage bead.
